recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. If the work group wants time-level precision restored or wants different consent effective-time modeling, that should be handled as a new decision because current source is internally consistent.
issue_request: FHIR-24897 was Published/Persuasive for FHIR-core Consent. It asked to clarify that the then-current Consent.dateTime element meant the date and time the consent instance was agreed to, not resource creation time, and to add a Consent.provision.period note describing the bound effective time of the consent in the base provision.
initial_application: Commit 2da480ca699986fa93ba5f234dc5b055146d8144 applied GF#24897 in the old Consent spreadsheet by changing dateTime from creation/indexing wording to agreement-time wording and by adding the requested provision.period comment and V2 mapping.
additional_context: Consent is active in source/fhir.ini. Later source refactoring moved the resource from consent-spreadsheet.xml to structuredefinition-Consent.xml; commit 89587cb0d9612f16695f4451d6653a53e300d846 changed Consent.dateTime to Consent.date with type date, commit d4aba66bf49bed3c8b5ccfc888c4d313c91913f3 added top-level Consent.period for consent-wide effective time, and the later FHIR-39597 reconciliation removed obsolete base-provision wording from Consent.provision.period.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source defines Consent.date as the agreement date, Consent.period as the consent-wide effective period, and Consent.provision.period as provision-specific with a comment pointing readers to Consent.period for consent-wide effective time. Re-adding dateTime or base-provision wording would contradict later current-build decisions.

related_jiras.note: Later Published/Persuasive Consent issue removed the provision-zero/base-provision model, which affects how the original provision.period note should be interpreted now.
